infeasible: WATER IS LETHAL, SO 'SWIMMABLE / RAMPED MOATS, CANALS, TRENCH RIVERS, QUAYS' CANNOT BE BUILT AS DESCRIBED. Any water surface that puts the body below -1.6 m triggers the tentacle drag and drowning of round 55 (src/systems/falls.ts: `onLand = inDungeon || pos.y > SEA`; src/systems/waterFall.ts; WATER in src/data/playTuning.ts; DECISIONS.md ~line 602). This hits Dagon (causeway), Charles (moat), Lilith, Zann, Mother Hydra and the Old Man. Real options: (a) shallow visual water sheets whose bed stays above -1.6 m, (b) a kerb with a `fall`/solid collider so the player never wades into deep water, (c) a hall-local water volume that is explicitly non-lethal (new tuning flag plus a test). Also decide how mounts, foe pathing (tactics/roam) and tests/enclosed audits treat it. Pick one in the plan before Phase 3.

PHASE 2 'SEA INLAND / sea:false' SPIKE IS THE WRONG SPIKE. `Biome.sea` is unused and the sea is one global plane (src/render/sea.ts, seaMask.ts). Nothing needs a per-biome switch. The real work is (1) `Pad` is only `circle | rect` and `flatten` takes one constant `level` (src/world/placements.ts ~96-98), so a ring/stepped/basin/ramp pad needs a new height-function pad kind, and (2) the drowned look needs terrain below -3 (terrainMesh skips cells below -3 and treats cells below `seaLevel - 1` as drowned; WORLD.seaLevel is -2). Re-scope the spike to 'pad with a height profile'.

CROWN make/keep distances of 220/280 m are invisible. RENDER.far is 140, FX.fogFar 132 (about 55 when mad), and chunks stream only 2 away (src/data/tuning.ts, src/render/worldScene.ts). The only working precedent, wayViews, uses MAKE 100 / KEEP 135. Set crown make/keep to roughly 100/135. Anything meant to read from afar (Kadath's domes, the Haunter's steeple, Dunwich storm, the star-cone city, Y'ha-nthlei) must be a skyline.ts silhouette (src/render/skylineShapes.ts), not a crown prop.

THE SOLID CEILING AT 6 m KILLS THE ABOVE-WALL ART IN 18 OF 27 HALLS. dungeonParts `ceiling()` adds a solid box at wall top (DUNGEON.height 6) in every roofed hall; only the 9 open-roof kits (hill, sunken, elder, tsath, onyx, cyclopean, fungoid, void and one more per kits.ts `roof:'open'`) have none. Keziah's 'beam roof stays' with folded panels / rafter fans / polyhedra above 6 m, Hypnos's dome iris, Zann's trusses and any 'tall lid' on a roofed kit are contradictory unless that hall's kit is switched to the shaft/open roof (a `roomKitId`-style per-hall override exists for `sunken`, `mine`). State per hall which roof it gets; do not list shaft for only some.

THE POCKET KEY IS INERT IN ROOFED HALLS. realmLook.indoors() only dims mist/haze/far; sky.update(enclosed) and skyline.update(enclosed) and dungeonFogOf neutralise region keys indoors. So a pocket key changes the sky only where the kit is open-roof: in practice Nyarlathotep (onyx) and Umr at-Tawil (void). Keziah, Hypnos and Zann (roofed) would show nothing. Either give them an open roof or draw the pocket sky on a hall-local dome/iris mesh. Also a recolour alone is thin against 'portals to boss dimensions': the plan has no walkable pocket, so 'dimension' is a skin over the same 48 m box.

SKINS MUST SUPPRESS THE EXISTING PITCHED ROOF. dungeonShell.roof() already raises a shingle roof (rise = min(7, w*0.62)) over every 'building' kit (timber, townhouse, church, marble), and mound kits get an earth cap/skirt/brow. A new crown or tall lid on those halls will clip or double the roof. The HallSpec needs a `roof: 'keep'|'none'|'replace'` field and a test, not just new code sites.

ONE DOOR SERVES ulthar_kadath: the Ulthar gate has the Leng (88 m) and Kadath (142 m) halls inside a single 176x128 rect (sites.probe). A separate 'Leng monastery precinct' and a 'Kadath citadel' on the same door cannot both be an exterior. Do one Ulthar exterior with two crowns (monastery roof, domes) and let the Kadath gate (hidden: minSeals, SEALS.kadath = 4) stay the only true portal.

DEMO BORDER LEAVES NO ROOM FOR SEVERAL EXTERIORS. Distance from the door to the demo mist (src/world/demoBorder.ts) measured: munoz 24 m, outsider 32 m, swamp_tomb (Voice) 16 m, hound 112, witch_house 84, alchemist 188. Munoz and Outsider are also only 24 m apart. A castle plus graveyard for the Outsider, a Munoz row, or a Voice 'marsh graveyard' cannot grow past the mist; the plan checked only Charles (188 m). Either keep those three to precinct-in-place dressing, or move the border check into the Phase 0 pad budget (HallSpec footprint <= distance to border minus blend 12).

HOUND / UNNAMABLE GEOMETRY: the Hound's door is about 52 m from the sea and region edge on its west and deserted_house is 20 m east (rect to rect). A 'necropolis filling the west' can only extend north and south. The 20 m Hound/Unnamable gap quoted by the plan is correct, so any shared burial ground must be one HallSpec precinct, not two.

TSATHOGGUA 'YOTH PIT BASIN PAD (30 m)' IS ALREADY INTERIOR ROOMS. Yoth is a pit room and red_yoth a hall inside an open-roof dungeon (dungeons/dungeonsFar); a second basin pad would overlap the dungeon's own rect pad and flatten the interior floors. Build the descent as the existing rooms' floor levels (roomLevel / `floorAt`), not a pad.

A PLINTH PAD NEEDS layout.base RAISED. `layoutDungeon(def, door, landHeight(door))` computes `layout.base` before the pad exists, and the pad is `{kind:'rect', rect: layout.rect, blend: PAD.dungeon (12), level: layout.base}`. A raised plinth for citadels/acropolises changes the base for every room and the door-to-hall levels, so it has to go into layoutDungeon, not the pad stage. There is also no terrain slope limit, so the stated 'feet-stop bands' rationale for stepped terraces is moot (they would just be decoration).

HALL AIR NEEDS A NEW SOURCE, NOT A GUARD LIFT. src/render/arenaAir.ts keys on `worldLayout().arenas.filter(a => a.air)` and returns at its top when `indoors` (worldLife passes `!outside`, outside = !enclosed && !!g.overworld). Lifting the guard gives nothing because halls are not arenas. Create a hall-air feed keyed by hall id and run it when enclosed. Only the 18 roofed halls lack ambient air; the 9 open-roof halls already receive weather, fauna and arenaAir-like drift through `enclosed === false`, so exempt them from the air budget and from the rain/lightning conflict below.

GroundFx.steady MARKS SHARE THE 256-DECAL CAPACITY WITH TELEGRAPHS (src/render/decals.ts CAPACITY 256; groundFx MAX 56). The plan's sigil rings, rune circles, plates, tide lines and rite marks per hall would starve boss telegraphs in a fight. Add a per-hall steady budget (for example 24 of 56) and a test that the boss telegraph reserve is never below its worst case.

hallViews MUST INVERT wayViews' GATING. wayViews and arenaAir are hidden when enclosed (worldLife.update: `ways.update(camera.position, time, !outside)`). A hallViews copy has to be shown only when in that hall and enclosed or open-roof-in-hall, and it needs its own lamp slot budget: only 12 lamp slots, MAX_HALOS 400, LIGHT_NERVES shared. Also the key collision is real: worldScene does `slicer.add(-1 - k, ...)` and `lights?.add(-1 - k, ...)` while signViews uses `LIGHT_KEY = -1`; hallViews must take a distinct negative range or a string key.

PHASE ORDER IS BROKEN. Phase 4 (Voice exterior) needs `graveField` from Phase 6; the 'maze' plan used by Phase 5 does not exist in Phase 2's list; Phase 0's empty spec files contradict CLAUDE.md 'never scaffold later phases' and 'files under 300 lines with one responsibility'. Each phase should land with the first consumer. Also the proposed test name `pads.test.ts` collides with the existing gamepad test file; name it `hallPads.test.ts`.

WILBUR: the boss hall is the 'upstairs' room (+4 m, reached by the loft stair from the kitchen) and a separate 'barn' hall room already exists in the same dungeon. A 'barn nave' boss hall contradicts the room graph and duplicates the barn. The boarded upper floor with the Whateley hole is the truer fit. The plan also lists Wilbur under Shaft Halls in one place and under Living Houses in another; pick one.

FAMILY OVERLAP. Of the 27 hall bosses, eleven are still house-kind places after the plan (the owner's 'why only houses?'), and eight use the same tall-lid shaft / dome / drum skin. At least one of 'Living Houses' and 'Shaft Halls' has to be thinned or the owner will see the same silhouette repeated.

SCHEDULE. 14 phases at 5-6 months solo is optimistic given the audits (npm run audit: dungeon walks, rayAudit, objectAudit, enclosedAudit, bossStand, soak with all 27 halls changed). 9-14 months is the honest range unless the plan cuts to about 10 shipped halls first. Every new precinct needs tests/enclosed.test.ts entries and a rayAudit pass, which the phases do not budget.
lore: Curwen: the panelled portrait that hides the passage belongs to the Olney Court house in Providence (the Pawtuxet bungalow/farm is the lab and vault). Do not put the portrait in the Pawtuxet hall; use Olney Court's library, or keep the game's own placement and say so in DECISIONS.md.

The Shining Trapezohedron cannot be a '7-face polyhedron': a trapezohedron has an even number of faces. Lovecraft's stone is an irregular many-planed crystal held by seven bands in a hinged metal box, in the Starry Wisdom church (the Haunter). Use 'seven bands' for the box and an even-faced shape for the crystal.

Ephraim Waite / Asenath Derby: the Waite house is in Innsmouth, the Derby house is in Arkham. 'Twin houses across a lane' merges two towns. The dungeon is the Waite house only; Derby's study can be a room, not a second building across a lane.

The god-faces are carved on Ngranek (Oriab, the Dreamlands), not on Kadath. The 'carved faces on Kadath' crown should be Ngranek's face in the skyline or Kadath's onyx castle with its stairs and the unseen Great Ones.

A Devil Reef causeway for Dagon is invented: the story says the reef is about a mile and a half offshore (Innsmouth) and Dagon of 1917 is a Pacific islet with a monolith and carved cyclopean ground. A temple at the west end with a causeway to a 'mouth' is acceptable as the game's own geometry (the coast is about 124 m east of the rect, the temple is 88 m from the mouth), but label it invented, and keep the monolith and the bas-relief as the true motifs.

Wilbur Whateley dies in the Miskatonic library, but the game already stages the arrival in the barn and the fall in the library (data/cutscenesBoss.ts, cutscenesFall.ts). A Dunwich farmhouse with the sealed upper floor, the 'tracks', the sentry hills and the Sentinel Hill stone circle is the true motif; the Dunwich Horror's ritual stones belong to the open arena, not to the farm.

The Whisperer (Henry Akeley): the aerial mast and tin shed are invented; the story has a farm on a hillside above a brook, the study with phonograph and cylinders, and the Mi-Go canister. Pigeons for the Haunter and frogs for the Voice are not in the critter list (src/data/fauna.ts CRITTER_IDS) or the stories (Haunter: the church interior, dead birds in the belfry? no; Voice: the Mad Man's cult swamp). Use bats and moths for the church and fireflies for the swamp, which exist.

The Hound of Tindalos hall is a graveyard in the game, but the Hound's churchyard in the story is Dutch, in Providence (Dr. Dexter), not a medieval sprawl; for the Hound of Tindalos itself, the angles are the motif (acute-angle corners), not tombs. The plan's 'necropolis' for the Hound should be named by the game's own chapel (Hound is Dunsany/Long/Moore adjacent) and noted as a game invention.

UNVERIFIED AGAINST SOURCE AND SHOULD BE CHECKED BEFORE COMMITTING TO ART: Ghatanothoa's hooded priests and Mu temple (Lovecraft/Bishop: the mountain Yaddith-Gho and the carved stairs), Rhan-Tegoth's museum layout (Bishop/Lovecraft: Alaskan ice, a stone room with a red-eyed idol), Hypnos's studio (Lovecraft: the sculptor's room; no dome), Leng's monastery interior (Lovecraft: the High Priest Not to Be Described, yellow mask, windowless stone monastery), and the Alchemist's moat (Lovecraft: a castle in a lonely forest, no moat). The High Priest's flute belongs to Azathoth's court in the Dreamquest, not to Leng's priest; the game's use is its own invention.

FIX A REAL WRONG-STORY REFERENCE: src/data/epitaphs.ts line 26 reads 'Hyde tomb' for a great horror; Hyde is the tomb in 'The Tomb' with Jervas Dudley, not the Voice/Unnamable cemetery. Confirm which horror it sits under and rename the tomb to the right story.

Kadath: the Great Ones' castle is onyx on a plateau in the cold waste, approached by the Dreamlands' dream-stair; the game's hall uses hidden_platforms with a starfield floor, which is fine, but a 'citadel with domes seen from Ulthar' contradicts the text, where Kadath is never visible from the lowland towns.

Nyarlathotep and Azathoth are outer gods: Azathoth sits in the black chaos with idiot flute players; a hall for him is an open chaos with flute-playing shapes, not a throne room. The plan's 'Azathoth' spec should drop a built throne and keep drifting platforms plus a pulse.
alike: Three farmsteads on one template: Curwen (Pawtuxet), the Whisperer (Vermont), Wilbur (Dunwich). Differentiate by layout (courtyard, hillside, long barn plus house) before art.

Three or four castles on the same `setShapesCitadel` family: Charles Dexter Ward's castle-like Curwen-style house, the Outsider's castle, the Great Ones' castle and the High Priest's tower. Their keep/curtain/tower module is the same shape set with different colours.

Four graveyards: the Hound, the Unnamable, the Voice (marsh) and the Outsider (castle graveyard) all use `graveField`. Give each a distinct plan (grid, tilted headstones, crypt avenue, drowned plots).

Five void/starfield pockets: Keziah, Nyarlathotep, Umr at-Tawil, Hypnos and Zann. Great Ones and Umr already share the hidden_platforms starfield floor. Without a walkable difference they read as five recolours of the same dark box.

Four water-sheet halls: Dagon, Mother Hydra, the Shoggoth and Lilith. One hall water shader and a flood hook (floodDepth 0.7, floodSlow 0.35) do them all; the plan should say which has a deck, which has a causeway, which has a canal.
Six 'eyes follow / faces turn' devices: Charles, Ephraim, Hypnos, the Old Man, the Great Ones and Ghatanothoa. Same animated-face prop with different skins; limit it to two or three halls.
Mirrors recur: the Outsider, Ephraim, Lilith and Charles. One mirror prop with different frames.
Six lab-apparatus halls (Curwen, Charles, Munoz, the Shunned house, the Whisperer, Rhan-Tegoth): coils, jars, pipes. Share one kinetic kit.
Sliding panels or shutter-type reveals appear in the Whisperer, Nyarlathotep, the Polyp and Ghatanothoa; one animated-panel kit.
Tall-lid shaft/dome/drum skins appear in eight halls.

Eleven of the halls are still house-kind places (the owner's 'why only houses?' was not fully answered): Curwen, Charles, Ephraim, Munoz, Wilbur, the Whisperer, the Witch's house, the Alchemist, Hypnos, the Shunned house and the Haunter.
missing: No main boss is missing. The 27 hall bosses plus brown_jenkin, mother_hydra, nyarlathotep and curwen_pit_thing are all named. yeb belongs to the Nug open arena, and there are 19 open-arena sites, which are round 61-63 houses; the plan correctly leaves them out.

There is no walkable accompanying area or real boss dimension. Every plan item is a skin over the same 48 m box (3x3 cells at 16 m, arena radius 23). The only true portal in the game is the existing Kadath gate. If the owner wants 'portals to boss dimensions', the plan needs at least one hall that is actually a separate walkable region (a pocket region with its own entry, save position and demo-border behaviour, tested by the footingSafe fallback in src/systems/save.ts).
Dungeon entrances and doors (src/data/doors.ts, doorViews, doorShapes) get no design: every dungeon's door look stays per-kit, so a Dagon causeway or a Kadath stair does not change how it is entered.
No counter-plan for the demo border (munoz 24 m, outsider 32 m, swamp_tomb 16 m from the mist) and for region-edge and sea placement (hound about 52 m from the sea).

No handling of weather, lightning and moon shadow under domed or skinned open-roof halls. The 9 open-roof halls get rain and lightning through `enclosed === false`, so a dome, drum or a replacement lid there lets rain, strikes and the moon's shadow map pass straight through it. Needs `Layer`-style occlusion or a per-hall 'covered' flag that feeds weather.update, lightning.update and moonShadow.

Cutscene and camera clamps are only gestured at: the arrival and fall scenes (cutscenesBoss, cutscenesMore, cutscenesRest, cutscenesDeep, cutscenesFall) assume the old 48 m box. A crown, a raised plinth or a taller hall changes the camera collision and the shot lines; each needs a cinemaPlan check.

No saves-compatibility note: saves restore position behind a `footingSafe` check and fall back to the checkpoint. Raising a plinth or lowering a basin pad changes the ground under old saves; the plan needs a test that a pre-change save inside a changed hall is moved to a safe footing.

No test for the 'two Outer Gods in halls' fact (see corrections) or for seal order: SEALS.after (yog_sothoth after umr_at_tawil, azathoth after yog_sothoth) and the hidden Kadath room (`minSeals` 4) depend on hall access that a precinct could break by moving a door.
corrections: Umr at-Tawil is also tier `outer_god` (src/data/roster.ts), so Nyarlathotep is not the only Outer God in a hall; the plan's 'the outer god pocket' wording should cover Umr and, by the seals chain, Yog-Sothoth and Azathoth.
Keziah's `arena_reconnect` hook runs from phase 1; only `camera_warp` begins at 0.5. The plan puts both at 0.5.
The Polyp also has the `decoys` hook; the plan omits it when it lists the Polyp's reality tricks.
The repo is at round 64 (see worldLife.ts 'createVigilMarks ... round 64'), not 63. Name the plan's phases as round 65 onward.

VERIFIED CORRECT (no change): the Hound/Unnamable rect gap of 20 m; the 28-dungeon count; the 59 baked models; the lights-key collision (worldScene `slicer.add(-1 - k, ...)` and `lights?.add(-1 - k, ...)` against signViews `LIGHT_KEY = -1`); the main.ts line references for region/enclosed passing; Dagon's 88 m temple-to-mouth and the ~124 m coast gap (the plan's causeway length holds).

Baysof / corners: roomStyle `baysOf` buttresses are 1.4 m deep and +/-0.7 m wide at +/-8 and +/-16 along each wall, so the four corner spandrels (about 9.5 m on the diagonal) are free for the plan's corner features. No change needed.
Brown Jenkin's script uses the `joins: {with, below}` field (src/data/schema.ts); the plan's Brown Jenkin / Keziah pairing must keep `joins` or the second body stops spawning in the hall.

Boss spawn is spread around the room centre by `spread` = 6 m (wide hall) or 2.5 m (otherwise), and the arena is `{x, z, radius: r.half - DUNGEON.wall}` = 23 m (src/world/roomFurnish.ts ~61-67). Any new centre feature (pit, altar, pool, loom, plinth) must stay out of the +/-6 m spawn strip and the 23 m radius; hallSet's rules (`SET_RULES.inner` 0.78, the 5 m cap `p.h <= DUNGEON.height - 1` in tests/hallSets.test.ts) already enforce this for props, so HallSpec features should go through hallProps, not around it.

Replace the plan's 'camera at 220/280 m' and 'swim through a moat' language, and the 'Phase 2 sea:false spike', with the measured limits above (far 140, fog 132/55, lethal water below -1.6, global sea plane, pad constant level).
